newsitem.title: USA: Alco Q1 margins down from acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Alco Q1 margins down from acquisitions.

text.p: Alco Standard Corp said Thursday that margins declined to 7.1 percent this quarter from 7.6 percent in last year's first quarter, mostly from the short-term dilutive effect of IKON Office solutions's rapid acquisition of technology services companies and transformation expenses in Europe.

"IKON's outstanding results continue to reflect our ability to achieve significant internal growth, while also expanding our business through an aggressive acquisition effort," said John E. Stuart, Alco's chairman and chief executive. "While posting internal revenue growth of 15 percent for the quarter, IKON acquired 23 companies with annualized revenue of approximately $170 million."
Revenues for fiscal 1997's first quarter grew 27 percent to $1.14 billion.
The company said the results reflect a very strong performance from the company's traditional copier business with substantial growth in both equipment placements and copy volume.

Stuart said that of the 23 acquired companies 10 were systems integrators, seven were outsourcing companies, and six were traditional copier dealers. The increasing number of systems integration and outsourcing companies in the acquisition mix reflects IKON's intention to strengthen its ability to offer customers a complete office technology solution, from traditional copier systems to computer networking and outsourced imaging and duplicating services.

Including discontinued operations, Alco reported $53 million in net income and $0.36 earnings per share for the fiscal 1997 first quarter. Discontinued operations represent Unisource Worldwide Inc. (UWW), which began operating as a separate public company on January 1, 1997.
